title: Word: Edit with Copilot for users in Microsoft 365 GCC
summary: Hold: the Anthropic configuration path skips the required acceptance of terms. The briefing also treats Claude availability in GCC editing as undocumented, although Microsoft's GCC-specific page currently restricts the model picker to Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the arrival default for Edit with Copilot in Word in GCC.
claims.quote: Searched: Edit with Copilot Word GCC default enabled rollout admin switch government. Read service description, government overview and Office editing help; release-note excerpts give a general Word default for another roadmap item, not a GCC arrival default.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft's government overview says Copilot operates entirely within the customer's U.S. government cloud tenant.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot is available in GCC, GCC High, and DoD, and operates entirely within the customer's U.S. government cloud tenant.
claims.fix: Add to the Data exposure bullet: 'However, Microsoft's GCC-specific Anthropic page says enabling those models processes Customer Data outside Microsoft's FedRAMP-authorized U.S. Government cloud.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/anthropic-non-federal-gcc. Narrow the risk rationale's 'inside existing Copilot licensing and cloud boundaries' to 'subject to existing Copilot licensing; the GCC editing data boundary is not yet confirmed'.

claims.claim: Microsoft's government overview says prompts, responses and generated content stay in the government cloud.
claims.quote: Prompts, responses, and generated content stay in the government cloud.
claims.fix: Qualify this general statement with: 'The GCC-specific Anthropic documentation gives an exception: when enabled, those models process Customer Data outside Microsoft's FedRAMP-authorized U.S. Government cloud.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/anthropic-non-federal-gcc; this is the same qualification needed for the preceding tenant-boundary claim.

claims.claim: The licence options page lists eligible US Government prerequisite plans for the Copilot add-on in GCC, GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot is available as an add-on in Government Community Cloud (GCC), Government Community Cloud High (GCC High), and Department of Defense (DoD) environments for the following plans.

claims.claim: The service description and licence options pages state no price for this capability.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot GCC government price Edit with Copilot pricing; Microsoft 365 Government Copilot GCC pricing price per user. Read the full service description and licence options pages; neither states a price for this capability.

claims.claim: Those two licensing pages state no meter or credit rate for this capability.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot GCC government price Edit with Copilot pricing. Read the full service description and licence options pages; neither assigns a meter or credit rate to Edit with Copilot.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Licences can be assigned in Microsoft 365 admin center through Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Billing > Licenses page. Select a product. On the product details page, select Assign licenses.

claims.claim: The printed Set-MgUserLicense command assigns a licence through the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: The PowerShell route needs the User.ReadWrite.All permission scope.
claims.quote: Assigning and removing licenses for a user requires the User.ReadWrite.All permission scope or one of the other permissions listed in the 'Assign license' Microsoft Graph API reference page.
claims.fix: Change 'PowerShell needs User.ReadWrite.All' to 'PowerShell can use User.ReadWrite.All' in the first row's note, and change the prose to 'the PowerShell route can use the User.ReadWrite.All permission scope and requires a UsageLocation on each user'. The cited page permits alternative assignment permissions.

claims.claim: A UsageLocation must be set on the user before licence assignment.
claims.quote: You can only assign licenses to user accounts that have the UsageLocation property set to a valid ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

claims.claim: The GCC Anthropic configuration path proceeds directly from Anthropic to Choose which users can access Anthropic models.
claims.quote: Review the information in the Terms and conditions section, and if they're acceptable, select the I acknowledge and agree to the above terms checkbox.
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].ui.path and the rendered path with 'Copilot > Settings > View all > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors > Available subprocessors for your organization > Anthropic > Terms and conditions > I acknowledge and agree to the above terms > Choose which users can access Anthropic models'. Keep https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/anthropic-non-federal-gcc as the docs link.

claims.claim: Changing the GCC Anthropic setting requires AI Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be a member of the AI Administrator or Global Administrator role to perform this task.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The setting is for non-federal GCC only; Claude is unavailable for federal GCC, GCC High and DoD customers.
claims.quote: Claude models aren't available for federal customers in GCC or for any customers in GCC High and Department of Defense (DoD) environments.

claims.claim: The non-federal GCC Anthropic setting has been available since 22 July 2026.
claims.quote: As of July 22, 2026, a new setting is available in the Microsoft 365 admin center that allows non-federal customers in Government Community Cloud (GCC) to use Anthropic models.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API for configuring the Anthropic provider setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph beta Copilot AI providers Anthropic subprocessors settings API; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph/api Anthropic provider Copilot settings beta. Read GCC and general subprocessor pages and both search results; no configuring API was documented.

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft does not state whether the GCC version of Edit with Copilot offers Claude.
claims.quote: Currently, those models appear as an option in the dropdown model picker only in Copilot Chat in the Microsoft Copilot app and on the web.
claims.fix: Replace the GCC model-availability caveat and corresponding open question with: 'Microsoft's GCC-specific page currently documents Anthropic models only in the model picker in Copilot Chat in the Microsoft Copilot app and on the web, not in Edit with Copilot.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/anthropic-non-federal-gcc. Retain the provider row as a general Claude-access control, not a control over GCC editing.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft's general Anthropic page names Edit with Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps as an experience where users can select Claude.
claims.quote: In capabilities such as Edit with Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps or Researcher, users can select Claude.

claims.claim: The Anthropic tenant setting governs which users can access those models, rather than being a switch for Edit with Copilot as a whole.
claims.quote: Under Choose which users can access Anthropic models, select All users, or specify users and groups, and then select Save. To disable the use of Anthropic models, select No users in Step 5.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated a government-cloud rollout mechanism for this capability.
claims.quote: Searched: Edit with Copilot Word GCC default enabled rollout admin switch government. Read roadmap record, service description, government overview and Office editing help; no GCC-specific rollout procedure was stated.

claims.claim: The roadmap description does not state whether GCC edits are tracked, reviewable or reversible.
claims.quote: Edit with Copilot in Word is now available to users in Office 365 GCC, enabling government customers to work with Copilot as a co-creator directly in your document to create, refine, and transform documents more efficiently.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: No feature-specific administrator action or separate government-tenant switch for Edit with Copilot is documented yet.
claims.quote: Searched: Edit with Copilot Word GCC default enabled rollout admin switch government. Read roadmap, service description, government overview and Office editing help; no separate GCC editing switch or required deployment action appeared.

claims.claim: The Claude option does not appear in the admin center for excluded federal GCC, GCC High and DoD customers.
claims.quote: The option to use Claude models doesn't appear in the Microsoft 365 admin center for these government and sovereign cloud customers.
